review_candidates.description: Meter is scaling fast, and we’re redefining the future of enterprise networking. If you’re a network engineer who thinks support is maintenance mode, think again. This is where you’ll work on some of the most complex and varied network designs in the industry, in environments where no two challenges are the same. You’ll diagnose and fix difficult problems, influence product direction, and sharpen your skills across every layer of the stack. This isn’t a step down from engineering; it’s a step deeper into the craft with direct impact on how next-generation networks are built and supported. You’re not just solving tickets; you’re solving the hardest networking challenges. If you thrive on variety, love to dig into complex systems, and want to shape how networks are designed and supported, this role is for you. What success looks like Provide consistently high-quality technical service to customers, earning their trust through accuracy, responsiveness, and results. Deliver actionable product suggestions to our engineering team, shaping the next generation of Meter’s hardware and software. Strengthen the team through clear documentation, peer training, and engineering expertise that makes everyone better. We’ll know it’s working if You consistently tackle complex tickets, adapting accurately to the constant changes in priority that come with an active queue. You identify and deliver improvements to our existing processes that make the team more efficient. You act like an owner, constantly building your technical depth and sharing that expertise to elevate the entire team. What your day-to-day will look like Troubleshoot and resolve tickets spanning every layer of the network stack. Manage and support complex customer networks, almost entirely remotely. Identify and document product bugs, escalating them with clear reproduction steps. Create well-structured feature requests informed by real customer needs. Build and maintain documentation that shortens time-to-resolution for everyone. Who you are A “Swiss Army knife” of networking, fluent in wireless, security, WAN/LAN, routing, DNS, and more. Committed to improving the network experience for every customer, delivering solutions that just work. Analytical by nature; you’re comfortable with ambiguity and energized by solving unique problems. Calm under pressure, even in the fast pace of redefining an industry. Today, we build and deploy these networks at scale. Ambitious companies and enduring institutions like Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, rely on Meter to keep their thousands of employees and locations online and productive. Our bet with Meter is simple: we will all use the internet more than we do today. We believe we have the definitive networking stack in place to enable business to do so as seamlessly and reliably as any modern utility. Execute End-to-End Functionality Testing: Perform comprehensive pre-shipment validation, testing network throughput, VLAN segmentation, routing protocols, firewall policy enforcement, and storage volume availability prior to crating and shipping. Container & Platform Validation: Deploy, bootstrap, and validate baseline Kubernetes clusters across bare-metal and virtualized nodes, verifying container runtime health, CNI network plumbing, and persistent storage integration. Build & Optimize Deployment Runbooks: Formulate and refine step-by-step staging and commissioning procedures, identifying failure points in the lab so that field technicians can execute plug-and-play onsite activations with minimal engineering overhead. Server & High-Performance Storage: Practical proficiency provisioning enterprise compute (Dell PowerEdge) and enterprise storage fabrics (SAN/NAS, iSCSI, NVMe-oF, or NFS), including RAID configuration and out-of-band management (iDRAC). Kubernetes & Container Fundamentals: Practical experience installing, configuring, and verifying Kubernetes environments, container runtimes (containerd), and basic container networking/storage plugins. Pre-Deployment Diagnostics & Validation: Demonstrated ability to isolate physical and logical faults across Layer 1 through Layer 4 using CLI diagnostics, optics validation tools, and packet captures.
